fresh_validated_observations.topic: Oil-disruption persistence matched-control study materially strengthens the effective-deliverable-supply mechanism
fresh_validated_observations.label: SUPPORTED / REGIME-SPECIFIC / CROSS-EPISODE DEEPENING
observed_controls: 2019 Abqaiq/Khurais: EIA records an immediate roughly 5.7 mb/d crude disruption, about 6% of global supply, and the largest one-day crude-price increase in a decade. Saudi Arabia quickly restored production capacity, met customers partly from inventories/reduced refinery intake, and EIA records prices back near pre-attack levels by end-September/early October.

2021 Suez blockage: roughly 5 mb/d of oil and products normally used the Suez/SUMED route around that period. The blockage generated a sharp but short-lived oil-price reaction because the physical issue was a transit delay with an available Cape reroute and the vessel was refloated within days; price attention then reverted to OPEC+/demand.

2011 Libya: IEA estimated 132 million barrels of light-sweet crude had been removed by end-May and expected Libyan supply to remain largely unavailable for the rest of 2011. Grade-specific scarcity and persistence were large enough that IEA members released 60 million barrels, 2 mb/d for 30 days, explicitly to bridge the gap until replacement production arrived.

2022 Russia invasion: IEA initially estimated up to 3 mb/d could be shut in while only Saudi Arabia/UAE had substantial immediately usable spare capacity and OECD industry inventories were 335.6 million barrels below the 2017-2021 average, the lowest since 2014. This was a much less substitutable starting state and produced a more persistent global energy-price shock; emergency stock releases were historically large.

2026 Yanbu/Hormuz regime: the current Saudi disruption is physically real, yet benchmark Brent eased as alternative Gulf loadings and ship-to-ship exports near Sohar restored effective deliverability. At the same time, accessible replacement grades such as ESPO carried extreme premiums and freight/insurance remained stressed, showing scarcity rent can migrate across grade/location/freight instead of disappearing.
fresh_validated_observations.inference: Across qualitatively matched episodes, headline gross disrupted capacity is insufficient to forecast price persistence. The stronger causal state vector is expected outage duration plus effective substitution capacity: inventories/emergency stocks, spare production, alternative routes, grade/refinery compatibility, freight/insurance capacity, and demand elasticity. When these buffers are credible, benchmark spikes tend to decay faster; when several buffers are simultaneously constrained, scarcity is more persistent and can spread into product/grade premiums.
alternative_explanations: Global demand regimes differ materially across 2005/2011/2019/2021/2022/2026.
Monetary policy, USD and financial positioning contaminate event-window price changes.
Emergency-stock announcements are endogenous responses to severe shocks, not independent treatments.
The present study is qualitative and not yet a timestamp-safe statistical event study.
fresh_validated_observations.falsification: Weaken the mechanism if a larger matched sample shows gross disrupted capacity predicts 5d/20d benchmark and physical-premium persistence at least as well as substitution/inventory/duration variables after controlling for demand and macro regime.
fresh_validated_observations.decision_support: Maintain WAIT on simple headline-driven Brent extrapolation. For future disruptions, prioritize effective deliverable supply and route/grade/product/freight controls before assigning a persistent inflation or commodity-price thesis.

fresh_validated_observations.topic: Daily equity big-move scan adds a clean positive fundamental-surprise control and a market-structure/valuation rumor candidate
fresh_validated_observations.label: BIG-MOVE LAB CANDIDATES

cases.move: about +8% on Sep. 18 while STOXX 600 fell about 1.1%
cases.observed_fact: LPP's primary release reported Q2 revenue +18% YoY in constant currencies to PLN6.6B, e-commerce +16.4%, gross margin +3.7 pp to 57.7%, EBITDA +42%, EBIT +57% and net profit +48% to PLN768M; the company raised 2026 gross-margin, EBITDA-margin and net-profit-margin targets. Market reporting put net profit above consensus.
cases.inference: The residual move versus a weak European tape is consistent with a genuine upward revision in expected earnings power driven by broad-based demand plus margin improvement, not merely factor beta. This is a useful positive matched control against Volkswagen's same-day negative estimate-reset gap.
cases.pre_move_predictor_status: The release itself is a catalyst, not a pre-move predictor. Earlier Q1 profitability improvement and expansion were public but did not mechanically imply the magnitude of the Q2 beat; no pre-release edge is claimed.

cases.move: about -11.3% on Sep. 18 versus FTSE 100 about -1.45%
cases.observed_fact: Market reporting attributed the move to reports that Airtel Money could target at least about $800M of IPO proceeds and an $8B-$9B valuation, lower than previously discussed targets. Trading volume was reported far above its recent average.
cases.inference: If confirmed, the price gap is consistent with a lower implied monetization/value realization for the fintech subsidiary and weaker external price discovery than investors had embedded. Because the key deal terms were attributed to unnamed sources and remain changeable, this is not promoted to a canonical causal case yet.
cases.unknown: No company-confirmed revised IPO terms were validated in this window.

LPP Sep. 18 +~8% versus STOXX 600 -~1.1%: clean positive earnings/margin-revision control, with no pre-release predictive edge claimed.
